parts.title: The Plan
parts.text: Ayesha unrolled a **schematic** across the workbench, a detailed diagram of the pedal-powered water pump she hoped would save the community garden. Gustav, who loved anything **mechanical**, traced the gears with his finger. Mei admired the **ingenuity** of using an old bicycle chain to drive the pump. "It will take all weekend to **assemble**," Ayesha said, tying back her hair.

parts.title: When Things Break
parts.text: The first test was a disaster. Water sprayed everywhere except into the bucket. Mei discovered a **flaw** in one pipe joint, and the group had to **troubleshoot** every connection, checking one after another. The leak was a big **setback**, and Gustav groaned that the garden would be brown by the time they finished. "Then let's **modify** the joint with a rubber seal," Mei suggested, digging through the toolbox.

parts.title: The Spark
parts.text: It took three weeks of **persistence**, and many ruined seals, before the pump finally pushed a steady stream into the bucket. It was a true **breakthrough**, and the three of them shouted so loudly that a neighbor knocked on the door. Ayesha also decided to **streamline** the design by removing two gears they did not need. The neighbor, a retired engineer, told them to file for a **patent**, the legal paper that protects an inventor's idea from being copied.

parts.title: The First Drawing
parts.text: That evening the pump watered the garden for the first time. Ayesha realized that inventing is mostly fixing, again and again, until something finally works. Gustav pinned the first drawing on the wall, not because it was perfect, but because it showed where the journey began.

definitions.meaning1: A legal document that gives an inventor the sole right to make and sell an invention for a set time. Example: The inventor filed for a patent so that no one could copy her design.
definitions.meaning2: To get this legal right for an invention. Example: She patented her design before showing it to investors.
